a21.speaker: Thomas Sankara (quoted)
a21.speech: "The slave who does not take charge of his own revolt does not deserve pity for his fate."

a162.speaker: Abdoulaye Mar Dieye, UN Assistant Secretary-General and UN Special Coordinator for Development in the Sahel
a162.speech: "We are here to listen, learn, recalibrate and refocus our collective efforts to achieve meaningful impact. How to recover one's dignity and one's future: that spirit was truly present in our discussion with His Excellency the Prime Minister and all the government ministers I met, and I want to reiterate once again the strong and powerful commitment of the United Nations system to stand alongside Niger." ; Noted that Niger and the Sahel are in the midst of reinventing their future: "What is happening in Niger is history unfolding and reinventing itself."

a162.speaker: Lamine Zeine, Prime Minister of Niger
a162.speech: Offered an overall overview of Niger's historical context and future aspirations, and stressed the urgency of achieving tangible impact through structuring projects by 2026, particularly in irrigation, security, and food and energy sovereignty, adding that youth, education, climate change and water management are also cross-cutting priorities.

a162.speaker: Yacoub El-Hillo, Regional Director for Africa, UN Development Coordination Office
a162.speech: "This is a moment to revitalise the partnership between Niger, its people and the United Nations. We want to see how we can adjust and change the way we work to align with Niger's priorities. The government owns the agenda. The government leads the agenda. We are here to accompany your efforts in order to realise the clear vision and mission you have for your great country."

a162.speaker: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
a162.speech: Announces an investment of $9 million to improve access to energy in Niger, a project aimed at strengthening the country's energy infrastructure to meet the population's growing demand for sustainable and reliable energy.

a264.speaker: 2012 RGP/H (General Population and Housing Census) and INS (National Institute of Statistics) data
a264.speech: According to the 2012 RGP/H, the population was estimated at 49,973 inhabitants; it is projected at 86,340 inhabitants in 2025 and 104,020 in 2030, according to INS data.

a264.speaker: Captain Harouna Ibrah, Delegated Administrator of the Rural Commune of Tanda
a264.speech: "The local economy, like that of the other communes of the department of Gaya, is doing relatively well despite the sanctions unjustly imposed on the country by ECOWAS" ; specified that in Tanda agriculture and fishing-related activities represent more than 80% of economic activity ; "The state, through its technical and financial partners such as UNDP, the Millennium Challenge Corporation and the Millennium Challenge Account (MCC/MCA-Niger), has supported women's farmers' organisations in Tanda and Sia in the processing and marketing of groundnut by-products."

a264.speaker: Captain Harouna Ibrah, Delegated Administrator of the Rural Commune of Tanda
a264.speech: Noted that, like the majority of the rural communes of the Dosso region, Tanda has no hygiene and sanitation service: "However, to ensure the upkeep of certain public places, the commune organises collective works with the support of youth and women's structures. The rubbish collected is then used by certain agricultural producers. As for the disposal of waste water or run-off water, the commune has no facilities provided for that purpose", he regretted.

a264.speaker: Captain Harouna Ibrah, Delegated Administrator of the Rural Commune of Tanda
a264.speech: Indicated that the main resource on which the commune relies is the municipal tax, whose mobilisation rests essentially on the commitment of village and tribal chiefs in collaboration with the municipal revenue collector: "However, since the appearance of armed bandits who carry out sporadic attacks in the area, the commune has been struggling to collect this tax. It is now limited to the revenues from market taxes and the subsidies granted by the state to ensure its functioning."

a264.speaker: Captain Harouna Ibrah, Delegated Administrator of the Rural Commune of Tanda
a264.speech: Issued an appeal to the population, inviting them to cultivate patriotism in order to foster genuine economic, social and cultural development of the commune.

a269.speaker: Minister of Communications and Digital Transformation of Mozambique
a269.speech: At the opening of the event, said that firm responses are needed for this type of crime [cybercrime].

a269.speaker: Francisco Mabzaia, Chairman of the Board (PCA) of EMME (Maputo Municipal Mobility and Parking Company)
a269.speech: says that, out of the roughly twenty million ideally required, the municipal company collects only four million from rotating parking, an amount insufficient to transform Maputo into a city of modern and intelligent systems.

a269.speaker: Pope Leo XIV
a269.speech: expresses solidarity with the victims of the earthquakes in Venezuela; the pontiff appeals for a strengthening of international humanitarian aid to the populations affected by the tragedy.

a269.speaker: Fishermen of Inhambane bay
a269.speech: acknowledge the increasingly pronounced reduction in shellfish and point to the growing pressure exerted on coastal and marine ecosystems.

a269.speaker: Residents of the village of Niarro, Natikiri neighbourhood, Nampula
a269.speech: denounce the increase in crocodile attacks that have already caused dozens of deaths; they therefore ask for the construction of a bridge to facilitate the crossing of people and goods.

a269.speaker: Population of Moma District, Nampula Province
a269.speech: asks the Government to rehabilitate the road linking Mogovolas District to the main town of that coastal region of Nampula Province.

a269.speaker: Traders of Moma District whose businesses still survive
a269.speech: state that it is very complicated to continue commercial activity because the route of about two hundred kilometres can take more than ten hours of travel.

a378.speaker: Jerónimo Cunha (Portuguese official, speaking at the Cape Verde-Portugal energy workshop)
a378.speech: Said that this opportunity can be taken advantage of, not only for Cape Verde to assert itself on climate issues, but also as an opportunity for the archipelago in economic terms. “Portugal looks at the energy transition as an economic opportunity. If we can produce our own energy with our own resources, we will be more competitive, and I think Cape Verde aspires to this, and this is what we want to contribute to and help Cape Verde with in this regard.” ; Said Portugal wants to share its experience with the archipelago at the level of energy consumers, “by their nature large consumers who deserve a different approach” regarding energy efficiency and renewable energies. “Portugal already has this status enshrined in its law, we already have some experience and we want, in effect, to share it with our Cape Verdean colleagues, so that they too can implement strategies and policies along these lines,” considering that large energy consumers by their nature must have mechanisms different from normal energy consumers.

a378.speaker: Rito Évora, Director of Industry, Trade and Energy of Cape Verde
a378.speech: Praised the existing cooperation protocol between the two counterpart institutions, arguing that it includes an important component directed at promoting the strategic axis of energy efficiency, as one of the axes of the National Programme for Energy Sustainability; stressed that this is an essential piece of the Cape Verdean energy transition programme, affirming that beyond replacing fossil energy sources with renewables, what can contribute most, and the cheapest and quickest way of avoiding greenhouse gas emissions, is reducing consumption by using energy more efficiently. “They are small investments, but with large impacts and a very short return in terms of recovering the investment.” ; Emphasised that the week is being marked by an intense agenda of debate and communication about energy, covering topics such as the integration of renewables, energy storage, micro-generation, a forum, and a German-Cape Verdean symposium.

a442.speaker: White House (statement)
a442.speech: According to a statement from the White House, the decision is part of Trump's broader effort to align U.S. foreign aid with his administration's priorities; the remaining USAID employees are expected to be laid off as operations wind down.

a649.speaker: Chen Zhihong, Ambassador of China to Mali (opinion column)
a649.speech: Writes that the United States has recently imposed customs duties, under various pretexts, on all of its trading partners, including China and African countries, seriously undermining the legitimate rights and interests of nations, violating WTO rules, harming the rules-based multilateral trading system and disrupting the stability of the global economic order ; argues the measures violate fundamental economic principles and market norms and that the use of tariffs as a weapon of extreme pressure is a typical example of unilateralism, protectionism and economic bullying, with the US pursuing “America First” and “American exceptionalism” under the cover of so-called “reciprocity” ; says the US is exploiting tariffs to overturn the existing international economic and trade order and sacrifice the legitimate interests of countries worldwide to serve its own hegemonic agenda.

a649.speaker: Chinese government
a649.speech: strongly condemns this measure and firmly opposes it.

a649.speaker: Wang Yi, Chinese Foreign Minister
a649.speech: posed the following questions: Has the trade deficit increased or decreased? Has manufacturing become more competitive or less competitive? Has inflation eased or worsened? Are Americans living better or worse?

a649.speaker: Chen Zhihong, Ambassador of China to Mali (opinion column)
a649.speech: Warns that the American tariff increase will disrupt global supply chains, raise production and logistics costs, distort market resource allocation, cause turbulence in financial markets and heighten recession risks ; says the tariff increase will undermine multilateral trade rules, noting that the WTO stipulates members must not unilaterally raise customs duties but settle disputes through negotiation, while the US has regularly bypassed the WTO, improperly invoking pretexts such as “unfair trade practices” to justify its protectionism, seriously damaging its international reputation.

a649.speaker: Chen Zhihong, Ambassador of China to Mali (opinion column)
a649.speech: Says Africa is also a victim of American unilateralism and protectionism: the imposition of customs duties disrupts the pace of the global recovery and inflicts unjustified shocks on the African economy; the renewal of the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) is becoming uncertain, “not to mention the brutal closure of USAID and the suspension of its ongoing projects,” all of which exacerbates the continent’s economic vulnerability.

a649.speaker: Chen Zhihong, Ambassador of China to Mali (opinion column)
a649.speech: Says that unlike the United States, China as a responsible developing country and the world’s second-largest economy will continue to open its doors ever wider, embodying an inclusive and mutually beneficial economic globalisation ; recalls that during the 2024 FOCAC Summit China announced zero-tariff treatment for 100% of tariff lines for least developed African countries maintaining diplomatic relations with it, and that China and African countries will strengthen cooperation in energy, infrastructure, mining, health and culture under the Ten Partnership Actions ; concludes that development is a universal right for all countries and not the privilege of a few, and that China is ready to cooperate with all friendly countries to adhere to genuine multilateralism, jointly oppose all forms of unilateralism and protectionism, and defend the international system with the United Nations at its core and the multilateral trading system centred on the WTO.

a695.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a695.speech: Accuses Ebrahim Rasool of being a "racialist politician" who "hates Donald Trump" and who stokes divisions; announced the decision on Friday 14 March on returning from a G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Canada, in an announcement made on X (formerly Twitter) relying on an article from the ultraconservative site Breitbart, justifying the expulsion by accusing the diplomat of stoking racial tensions.

a695.speaker: Breitbart (ultraconservative website)
a695.speech: Accuses Rasool of having made controversial remarks about American politics during a webinar organised by a South African think tank.

a695.speaker: Ebrahim Rasool, South African Ambassador to the United States
a695.speech: At that conference, analysed the rise of the MAGA (Make America Great Again) movement and the policies of the Trump administration through the lens of demographic change in the United States; denounced what he called a "supremacist assault" on diversity and inclusion policies; also criticised Elon Musk's rapprochement with the European far right, describing it as a "wake-up call" for a white community seeking protection; and, without directly attacking Donald Trump, advised South African diplomats not to "antagonise" Washington while calling for caution in exchanges with the American administration.

a695.speaker: Pretoria (South African government)
a695.speech: Judged this expulsion "regrettable" but reaffirms its will to maintain a constructive diplomatic relationship with the United States ; called on its diplomats to "maintain the established decorum in their interactions with the United States", while underlining its commitment to preserving a "mutually beneficial" relationship.

a695.speaker: Pretoria (South African government)
a695.speech: Firmly rejected Trump's accusations over the land expropriation law, stating that the law does not target whites and that Trump's declarations are "filled with disinformation and distortions".

a695.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a695.speech: Since his return to the White House in January 2025, has multiplied criticisms of the South African government, notably over a new land expropriation law which he and his ally Elon Musk denounce as an attack on the country's white minority; in February signed a decree suspending American aid to Pretoria and announcing an asylum programme for Afrikaners, descendants of European settlers, whom he describes as "refugees who are victims of racial discrimination".

a695.speaker: South Africa (complaint filed before the International Court of Justice, 2023)
a695.speech: Accused Israel of genocide in Gaza, a legal action that provoked the anger of the Trump administration, which firmly supports Israel.

a822.speaker: Eyob Tekalign (PhD), Ethiopia’s State Minister of Finance
a822.speech: Argues that some misconceptions about the Homegrown Economic Reform Agenda should be clarified and a consensus built around the economic reform programme that aims to correct imbalances and ensure a stable macro-financial system; says the points raised by some of the critics suggest a narrow interpretation of the reform agenda’s measures as well as the country’s growth trajectory, and that the role of investment (capital accumulation) in Ethiopia’s growth in the past decade is supported by numerous statistical evidence ; argues the reform agenda is fundamentally different – in timing, purpose and approach – from historical structural adjustment programmes associated with Bretton Woods conditionalities, because Ethiopia is launching its own reform programme on the back of continuing growth success: “This is not just a reform program with our backs against the wall, and some enforced move toward a ‘Washington Consensus’ in which the state’s role is pushed aside.”

a822.speaker: Eyob Tekalign (PhD), Ethiopia’s State Minister of Finance
a822.speech: Says it is important to correct an oversight some critics made associating the reform agenda directly to the initiatives of development partners, one making a specific mention of USAID’s new project, Advancing Economic Diversification in Ethiopia; states that the project is in its inception stage and is one of many that aim to support export competitiveness, and that “the government views and welcomes these kinds of projects as a complement to its reform efforts, not as its guidance tools. If our international friends in the East or West are willing to support our plans, we will welcome them.”

a822.speaker: Eyob Tekalign (PhD), Ethiopia’s State Minister of Finance
a822.speech: Says the reform plan is neither proposed nor imposed on Ethiopia by international institutions and that ownership of the agenda matters, expressing the hope that “the reform plan will rather be a broadly shared ‘Addis Abeba Consensus’”; warns that the Ethiopian economy is facing serious imbalances, with inflation running above 15 percent per year, foreign exchange severely rationed and the parallel market exchange rate premium well over 20pc.

a822.speaker: Abiy Ahmed (PhD), Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a822.speech: Recently put it that the reform plan, spearheaded by some of Ethiopia’s finest minds, is “Ethiopian through and through.”

a1123.speaker: Bassim Alawadi, Iraqi government spokesman
a1123.speech: A statement said the letter condemns "the Zionist entity's blatant violation of Iraq's airspace and sovereignty by using Iraqi airspace to carry out an attack on the Islamic Republic of Iran on 26 October".

a1123.speaker: Bassim Alawadi, Iraqi government spokesman
a1123.speech: Said the Iraqi foreign ministry would also bring up "this violation" in talks with the United States, Israel's close ally and top arms provider.

a1123.speaker: Iranian military
a1123.speech: Said some Israeli aircraft had fired a "small number of long-range missiles... from a distance", inside the US-patrolled airspace of Iraq.

a1123.speaker: Esmaeil Baghaei, Iranian foreign ministry spokesman
a1123.speech: Said Tehran was "sure that no neighbouring country has given this permission to the Zionist regime" to use its airspace ; "We certainly hope that our friends in Iraq will announce the necessary reactions, including by registering their protest with the United Nations, and will not allow such incidents to happen again."

a1123.speaker: Kataeb Hezbollah, Tehran-aligned group
a1123.speech: Condemned on Sunday the Israeli use of Iraqi airspace to attack Iran as a "dangerous precedent".

a1134.speaker: Aziz Haka, Epic Project Manager, Morogoro (FHI 360)
a1134.speech: Speaking after handing over the equipment worth 52 million shillings, said the provision of the equipment is part of supporting government efforts to improve health infrastructure in order to reduce new HIV infections and to encourage people to come forward for testing and to start ARV drugs ; "Along with providing medical equipment, FHI through the Epic project has been providing education about AIDS to young people and the community in general, and ensuring that treatment services reach people down to the community level."

a1134.speaker: Anneth Masawe, Supply Chain Supervisor of the Epic-FHI 360 Project
a1134.speech: Listed the equipment as including items for testing and preserving samples, cabinets for storing records, gloves, coats and rain boots, bags for carrying books and record documents, as well as other equipment for advancing HIV testing work; said the equipment will be delivered to 15 health facilities and will be used by community-level AIDS service providers so that they can easily reach the community and provide education and testing services.

a1134.speaker: Dr Best Magoma, Morogoro Regional Medical Officer
a1134.speech: Said the region has a total of 516 facilities providing HIV and AIDS services as well as 383 facilities for preventing mother-to-child transmission during pregnancy, delivery and breastfeeding; said that between January and September 2024, 406,045 people came forward for HIV testing at these facilities and of them 6,464 were found to have HIV infection and have started ARV treatment ; "The region, in collaboration with various AIDS stakeholders, has focused on targeted testing, partner and child testing, and network testing in order to reach national and international targets by 2030."

a1134.speaker: Adam Malima, Morogoro Regional Commissioner
a1134.speech: Said Tanzania has made great strides in the fight against HIV because in the beginning people were afraid to come forward for testing and stigma was high; however, he said that now the government, in collaboration with stakeholders, is hopeful that infections will reach zero in the coming days.

a1177.speaker: Olavo Correia, Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a1177.speech: Speaking to the press on the sidelines of the workshop on "Inter-island, International and Intermodal Connectivity and Digital Connectivity", stressed that the inclusion of Cabo Verde in this third MCC package reflects the recognition by the United States of America of the country and of the work carried out by Cabo Verdean generations over recent decades. He stressed that the "only priority" for Cabo Verde is connectivity and mobility in their various forms: "If we manage, with the support of the compact, to guarantee the best level of services, supply and governance with greater sustainability, and to place connectivity at the service of the diversification and the dynamic acceleration and economic management of Cabo Verde, we will, together with the United States of America, be rendering a great service to the Cabo Verdean nation, but above all to young Cabo Verdeans and to Cabo Verdean women on all the islands of Cabo Verde."

a1177.speaker: Olavo Correia, Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a1177.speech: Explained that the amount allocated to the compact will be defined at a later stage, after the projects have been presented: "After that, we will present it consistently, based on studies, based on analysis, with the involvement of the whole Cabo Verdean nation, and only then will we submit the justified envelope to the compact, and at that point we will then establish with the United States the amount that will be allocated to Cabo Verde."

a1177.speaker: Olavo Correia, Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a1177.speech: Underlined that at this moment the priority is to define the results to be delivered to citizens, as well as to focus on the necessary reforms, the projects to be developed and the objectives to be achieved, and emphasised the need for a strategic vision for the nation: "At this moment it is necessary to have the strategic vision, everyone's perception, to analyse the projects and fit them within the Government's vision regarding the future of the nation, which is to make connectivity and mobility a pillar for accelerating and amplifying opportunities in order to double the growth potential of the Cabo Verdean economy." He also highlighted the need to act in areas that are fundamental to overcoming the challenges, such as climate action, the digital transition, the diversification of the national economy and of the private sector, the improvement of the business and investment environment, and the development of human capital.

a1177.speaker: Joana Brito, coordinator of the Programme Development Unit (UDP)
a1177.speech: Explained that studies are currently being carried out in the areas of connectivity and mobility, with the constraints analysis phase already under way: "At this moment studies have already been launched in these two areas and they are at the stage of analysing the constraints." ; "The project preparation phase may take between 18 months and two years, and only after this time will the Government present them to the MCC board of directors and negotiate the package."

a1177.speaker: Joana Brito, coordinator of the Programme Development Unit (UDP)
a1177.speech: Stressed that the entire private sector will be directly involved in the process, as will all of civil society: "The entire private sector will be directly involved in this process, as will all of civil society, and this consultation modality will be implemented throughout this Compact development process."

a1295.speaker: Nelson Faria, PAICV (Cape Verde opposition party)
a1295.speech: States that, although Cape Verde has historically been a country of emigration, the phenomenon is taking on a different dimension and generating various consequences. "The immediate impact will certainly be the loss of manpower, some family breakdown. In the medium to long term there will probably be problems with our own social security; we will also have demographic problems, because it is people of productive age who are leaving. Another consequence that I believe is relevant concerns the country's capacity for self-assertion. When the country loses qualified people, valuable professionals, the country's standing will also tend to be called into question."

a1295.speaker: Afrosondagem (survey data)
a1295.speech: The latest Afrosondagem data reveal that 64% of young people aged between 18 and 35 intend to emigrate, with the search for employment being the main reason.

a1295.speaker: Zilda Oliveira, UCID (Cape Verdean party)
a1295.speech: Recalls that the latest Afrosondagem data show 64% of young people aged 18 to 35 intend to emigrate, and that the consequences are already being felt in various professional fields. "It is not only about university graduates; it ends up applying, for example, to civil construction, catering, hotels, areas linked to tourism. We are beginning to have a deficit. Our active population will shrink — about 50% of our active population are young people between 18 and 35. If those are the young people who intend to leave or who are leaving the country, I believe that in the short to medium term we will have a serious labour problem at various levels, which will impact the country's economic development and a range of responses in different areas."

a1295.speaker: MpD (Movement for Democracy, Cape Verde's governing party)
a1295.speech: Argues that youth emigration is not a recent phenomenon and that it has an impact on the national economy.

a1295.speaker: José Carlos da Luz, representative of the MpD
a1295.speech: Considers, however, that measures need to be taken to reverse the situation. "It is logical that this will bring a set of problems for the country. In fact, emigration is not only of young people with higher education; they come from various fields. This may also lead companies to think about increasing the wage bill in order to retain professionals. A shortage of metalworkers, plumbers, bricklayers, etc. is already being felt. But this is not a problem only for Cape Verde. Portugal also has this problem, with Portuguese people leaving for France and Luxembourg where they find better salaries. It is a situation that has to do with globalisation. I think that, for sure, Cape Verde will also soon be importing labour."

a1295.speaker: The political parties (PAICV, UCID, MpD)
a1295.speech: Believe that the study the Government intends to carry out on the "Aspirations of young Cape Verdeans residing in the country and in the Diaspora" could provide crucial data to define a national strategy that would allow the youth emigration scenario to be reversed.

a1432.speaker: Anambra State Government, in partnership with USAID, the Coca-Cola Foundation and TechnoServe
a1432.speech: Has reaffirmed its commitment to recycling plastic waste, securing more environmentally friendly solutions through strategic partnerships and innovative solutions.

a1432.speaker: Felix Odimegwu, Anambra State Commissioner for Environment
a1432.speech: Speaking while declaring open a stakeholders' meeting on Plastic Waste Recycling in Awka, Anambra State, said: "Plastic waste becomes a menace to the environment when not separated and channeled for recycling" ; highlighted the alignment of the Nigeria Plastic Solutions Activity with Anambra's strategic vision for sustainable development, adding that under the leadership of Governor Prof. Charles Soludo, Anambra has been actively pursuing initiatives to reduce waste, promote recycling, and foster a culture of sustainability ; announced the second season of the "All Anambra Communities Plastic Waste Recovery Challenge," aiming at reducing waste, promoting recycling, and creating employment for the residents, reinforcing the state's commitment to a cleaner, greener future.

a1432.speaker: Adesuwa Akinboro, Country Director of TechnoServe Nigeria (represented by Benneth Obasiohia, Senior Program Manager)
a1432.speech: In her remarks, emphasized the importance of collaboration in combating plastic pollution in the state; noted that the project sought to boost local economies and also create sustainable livelihoods, not forgetting Nigeria's significant contributions to global plastic waste, of which only 12 percent is being recycled in the country.

a1432.speaker: Professor Emma Ezenwaji, Chairman of the ASWAMA board of directors
a1432.speech: Gave a presentation on strategic partnerships for improved waste management service delivery in Anambra State.

a1432.speaker: Franklin Nwaribe, Senior Business Advisor
a1432.speech: Provided an overview of the Nigeria Plastic Solutions Activity.

a1471.speaker: USAID Malawi (statement dated January 24)
a1471.speech: has issued a statement that it is implementing some of the newly-elected US President Donald Trump's executive orders — on its part to do with the Reevaluating and Realigning US Foreign Aid. The statement is addressed to all USAID contracting & agreement officers and implementing partners, saying Trump's order follows an additional direction provided by the US Department of State.

a1471.speaker: Jami J. Rodgers, USAID senior procurement executive (statement)
a1471.speech: "USAID is pausing all new obligations of funding, and sub-obligations of funding under Development Objective Agreements (DOAGs), pending a review of foreign assistance programs funded by USAID." ; "The pause applies to applicable funding under all award instruments. Effectively immediately, contracting and agreement officers must not modify, extend, or exercise options or renewals for existing awards beyond the actions authorized below." ; "Contracting and and agreement officers shall immediately issue stop-work orders, amend, or suspend existing awards, consistent with the terms and conditions of the relevant award." ; "Following a review, contracting and agreement officers will communicate decisions related to whether an award will be continued, modified, or terminated with impacted contractors and recipients." ; "In addition, contracting and agreement officers must not issue new awards or release any new requests for proposals (RFPs), requests for application (RFAs), notices of funding opportunities (NOFOs), or any other kind of solicitation or request for foreign assistance funding until each activity has been reviewed and approved as consistent with the President's policy."

a1471.speaker: USAID
a1471.speech: indicates that the US Secretary of State has approved waivers of the pause under Trump's Executive Order, subject to further review, with respect to: 1. emergency food assistance and administrative expenses, including salaries, necessary to administer such assistance; 2. on a temporary basis, salaries and related administrative expenses, including travel, for all categories of personal services contractors; 3. legitimate expenses incurred prior to January 24, 2025, under existing awards or legitimate expenses associated with stop-work orders, suspensions, or pause-related amendments; and 4. exceptions to the pause approved by the Director of Foreign Assistance ; "The process for waivers, as well as the review process for activities, is forthcoming. Within 30 days, the Director of the Department of State's Policy Planning Staff (S/P) or its designate shall develop appropriate review standards to ensure that all foreign assistance is aligned with President Trump's foreign policy agenda. The review is to be completed within 85 days of January 24, 2025 [and] a copy of this notice has been posted to USAID's Implementing Partner Notices portals."

a1471.speaker: Al Jazeera
a1471.speech: reports that Trump's administration has announced a freeze on almost all new funding for foreign assistance programmes, with exceptions for allies Israel and Egypt. The report published today indicates that order from the US State Department yesterday also includes exceptions for emergency food programmes, but not health programmes that supporters say provide vital, life-saving services ; reports that the temporary freeze is slated to last for a period of at least three months and that in the first 85 days, Rubio is expected to make "decisions whether to continue, modify, or terminate programs".

a1471.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (memo)
a1471.speech: directed senior officials to "ensure that, to the maximum extent permitted by law, no new obligations shall be made for foreign assistance".

a1471.speaker: Humanitarian organisations
a1471.speech: immediately expressed alarm at the directive, voicing fears that it could contribute to global instability and loss of life.

a1471.speaker: Abby Maxman, head of Oxfam America (statement)
a1471.speech: "By suspending foreign development assistance, the Trump administration is threatening the lives and futures of communities in crisis, and abandoning the United States' long-held bipartisan approach to foreign assistance which supports people based on need, regardless of politics."

a1471.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (inaugural speech)
a1471.speech: confirmed the order to recognise only two genders, male and female, saying: "As of today, it will henceforth be the official policy of the United States government that there are only two genders, male and female."

a1471.speaker: US officials (Trump's team, as reported by international media)
a1471.speech: indicated that the order would impact federal documents including passports and would also block requirements at government facilities and at workplaces that transgender people be referred to using the pronouns that align with their gender; the definition of male and female will be based on whether people are born with eggs or sperm, rather than on their chromosomes.

a1689.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
a1689.speech: According to President Daniel Chapo, the central Mozambican province of Zambezia needs 1.5 billion meticais (about 23 million US dollars) to repair the damage caused by the post-election rioting. Speaking in Quelimane on Thursday, Chapo said that among the buildings attacked by rioters were schools, health units and the police commands in Morrumbala, Namacurra and Mocubela districts. He said he had visited several Zambezia districts "because of the violent, illegal and criminal demonstrations. There were huge losses in Zambezia calculated at 1.5 billion meticais".

a1689.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
a1689.speech: "We cannot destroy our own house", declared Chapo, "because tomorrow we may need the things that we are now destroying. People destroyed petrol pumps, and they woke up the following day to find that there was nowhere where they could refuel their cars". ; He claimed that the same people who had vandalised commercial infrastructures then tried to organise other demonstrations against food and fuel shortages and price rises which resulted precisely from the rioting they had stoked.

a1689.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
a1689.speech: Said the government is determined to carry out "structuring projects" in Zambezia, such as a bridge over the Licungo river in Mocuba district and a network of roads between the districts of the province - projects that were to have been paid for by the United States through the Millennium Challenge Account. Even though the US has withdrawn its support: "We are taking the decision that next year, come rain, come shine, with or without the MCA, we shall build the bridge and the roads", declared Chapo.

a1689.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of Mozambique
a1689.speech: Was confident that the project to build a new deep water port at Macuse will go ahead and provide a large number of jobs for young people in Zambezia. He added that the government is in discussions with the publicly owned rail and port company to transform the port of Quelimane into a reference port for developing the province, and also promised to bring industry back to Zambezia.

a1784.speaker: Omar Houssein Omar, President of the Tadjourah regional council and President of the National Association of Djiboutian Local Authorities (ANCLD)
a1784.speech: In his opening remarks, placed the emphasis on the financing of this project to strengthen the capacities of civil society organisations: “Within the framework of this civil society support project, the greater part of the financing, 90%, comes from the European Union and therefore 10% comes from the AIMF” ; “The various projects carried out so far have enabled us to change the mentality of our populations,” he told the representatives of the financial and technical partners ; stressed the importance of regional plans “emanating from different local authorities and localities” for the development of the populations of those areas ; told the audience that the establishment of concrete projects focused on food, hygiene, water and health would make it possible “to improve the living conditions of our populations from the country's rural areas”.

a1784.speaker: Omar Houssein Omar, President of the ANCLD
a1784.speech: “I therefore encourage, before handing over the floor, our financial partners to give priority to rural populations because that is where the needs are greatest, and to set up projects whose amounts are somewhat larger, because with small amounts one cannot carry out large projects,” before thanking the European Union and the AIMF for their contributions to the realisation of this project.

a1784.speaker: Schlede Simona, Head of Cooperation of the European Union Delegation in Djibouti
a1784.speech: Said this workshop would allow civil society organisations to exchange on “their challenges and opportunities to contribute to dialogue and policy reflection on inclusive and sustainable development” ; indicated that her organisation works in close collaboration with the Djiboutian authorities “to foster synergies and complementarity of our objectives and actions in line with Vision 2035” ; stressed the importance of this project implemented by the AIMF to strengthen the contribution of Djiboutian civil society organisations to governance and local development, which in her view allows the strengthening of the institutional and advocacy capacities of Djibouti's umbrella association as well as of civil society organisations, “with a view to preparing them to participate meaningfully in local decision-making processes and in the drafting and implementation of local development public policies”.

a1784.speaker: Schlede Simona, Head of Cooperation of the European Union Delegation in Djibouti
a1784.speech: “In order to support the dynamism of Djiboutian civil society organisations as development actors, a call for project proposals will be launched with an amount of approximately EUR 450,000,” declared Ms. Schlede.

a1823.speaker: Lucy Tamlyn, Ambassador of the United States of America to Benin
a1823.speech: "In a few months, the Arm 3 and Ancre projects will pack their bags, leaving behind impressive statistics," revealed the Ambassador. The diplomat explained that the project for Accelerating the Reduction of Morbidity and Mortality due to Malaria (Arm 3) contributed to a substantial reduction in hospital malaria fatality rates, which fell from 12.3 percent in 2011 to 0.9 percent in 2016, thanks to the expansion of triage, assessment and emergency treatment (Tetu). As for the project for Improving Reproductive, Newborn and Child Health (Ancre), the diplomat elaborated, it supports 90 percent of all registered public and private clinics in its ten health zones. The Ancre project also contributed, she continued, to qualifying 90 percent of the health zones as meeting WHO preparedness criteria for the Ebola virus response, making these zones better able to detect and respond to epidemics, notably Lassa fever. "This work has had a significant impact on both individuals and the health system," she confided. By way of illustration she referred to the situation of Mrs Sabi Adama, a mother of six living in a village far from Tchaourou, who nearly died during her third childbirth and who in 2017 decided to approach a community health worker recently trained with the support of Arm 3 and Ancre for advice during her new pregnancy: "She thus received prenatal care, intermittent presumptive treatment for malaria, and even breastfed her baby girl for six months." She announced that this day marks the end of the two projects but also the beginning of other large-scale programmes drawing on the experience of the projects now being completed.

a1823.speaker: Alassane Séidou, Minister of Health of Benin
a1823.speech: "The government of Patrice Talon, through my voice, would like to thank the government of the United States of America for the two ending projects and then to wish for their renewal or the development of new projects for better ownership and sustainability of the results."

a1823.speaker: Alassane Séidou, Minister of Health of Benin
a1823.speech: Taking stock in turn of the Ancre project, credits it with, among other things, the development of the strategic plan of the Health Emergency Operations Centre (Cous) and its equipping with furniture and office equipment, and the establishment of 239 quality-of-care improvement teams in public and private health facilities as part of implementing the national policy on quality assurance of care. Regarding the Arm 3 project, the Minister praised the establishment of an information and logistics management system for antimalarial drugs, which facilitated real-time decision-making and improved the availability of malaria commodities, as well as the establishment of the national malaria control policy through the introduction of Tpi 3 and injectable artesunate. On the basis of this positive record the minister called on his colleagues and other partners to show more courage and determination in order to guarantee every Beninese woman and man better health.

a1831.speaker: Harry Mukaka, National Bank of Malawi plc head of treasury and investment banking division (internal memo dated January 3 2025)
a1831.speech: Said the new guidelines removing pre-approved forex limits on customers' Visa cards have been introduced to facilitate the smooth processing of foreign exchange transactions; the memo reads in part: "It is imperative that all relevant staff members are informed of these changes and adhere to the updated procedures."

a1831.speaker: Phillip Madinga, Bankers Association of Malawi (BAM) president and Standard Bank plc chief executive
a1831.speech: Referred the matter to BAM executive director Lyness Nkungula.

a1831.speaker: Lyness Nkungula, Bankers Association of Malawi executive director (non-response)
a1831.speech: Was yet to respond to the newspaper's questionnaire on the rationale behind this measure and whether all banks have done the same.

a1831.speaker: Symon Yohane, Crossborder Traders Association of Malawi president
a1831.speech: Described the guidelines as unfair: "We are not happy with this directive because as traders, sometimes receive orders to supply at a short notice even in government departments."

a1831.speaker: Babra Banda, National Association of Business Women executive director
a1831.speech: "On face value, removal of pre-approved limits should mean this is an open cheque on foreign currency expenditure, but in the current context, this is a control mechanism which will further fuel black market transactions."

a1831.speaker: John Kapito, Consumers Association of Malawi executive director
a1831.speech: Said the guidelines are retrogressive, considering that Malawi opened up to e-markets that allow one to import and do international business by using a card and travel with less restrictions.

a1904.speaker: Office of the Prime Minister of Israel (statement)
a1904.speech: Reported on Saturday, in a statement, that Benjamin Netanyahu and Steve Witkoff, the United States special envoy for the Middle East, would meet today for that purpose, and that Witkoff would then hold discussions during the week with the Prime Minister of Qatar and senior Egyptian officials.

a1904.speaker: Hamas
a1904.speech: On Sunday, accused Israel of violating the ceasefire agreement because not all of the agreed humanitarian aid was entering the Palestinian enclave, in particular medicines, tents, fuel, foodstuffs and heavy machinery.

a1904.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a1904.speech: According to the UN, at least in the first week that number was exceeded; the UN warned that the aid faces enormous logistical distribution challenges amid tonnes of rubble and unexploded ordnance.

a1904.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Prime Minister of Israel
a1904.speech: Before his departure for the United States, said that he and Trump would discuss "victory over Hamas, achieving the release of all the hostages and dealing with the Iranian axis of terror in all its components", referring to Iran's alliance with militant groups across the region, including Hamas.

a1943.speaker: National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) of Ghana
a1943.speech: In a landmark announcement following a one-day forum in Kumasi, unveiled ambitious plans to overhaul the country's healthcare system, highlighting key reforms aimed at improving service delivery and efficiency under the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS).

a1943.speaker: NHIA officials
a1943.speech: According to NHIA officials, the proposal for a ten-year renewal period for health insurance cards aims to streamline administrative processes and ensure continuous coverage for beneficiaries across Ghana.

a1943.speaker: Theo Owusu Ansah, NHIA Director
a1943.speech: Addressing the forum, underscored the NHIA's commitment to achieving universal health coverage through a comprehensive implementation plan, which will be submitted to Parliament for approval and which outlines strategies for enhanced public recognition, prioritization of claims, and streamlined credentialing processes.

a1943.speaker: Theo Owusu Ansah, NHIA Director
a1943.speech: Revealed that the NHIA has already saved 9.5 million cedis by optimizing dialysis services, demonstrating the potential for substantial cost savings across the healthcare sector.

a1943.speaker: Dr Ernest K.P Kwarko, Board Chairman of NHIA
a1943.speech: In response to queries from journalists regarding drug efficacy and distribution, assured journalists that the NHIA is committed to rigorous quality assurance standards, emphasizing monthly payments totaling 12 million cedis to Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital as part of ongoing service agreements.

a1943.speaker: Local chiefs attending the forum
a1943.speech: Stressed the importance of public education campaigns to discourage self-medication practices and reduce politically charged debates surrounding healthcare policies on media platforms.

a2355.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (report released 6 October 2020)
a2355.speech: States that Ethiopia has an increasingly high need for humanitarian assistance, estimated at more than 1.4 billion dollars, due to the compounded issues of the COVID-19 pandemic, locust invasions, conflict and floods, and that despite rising needs the funding gap is larger than it has been in a decade, amounting to 773.9 million dollars; projected that malnourished children and pregnant and breastfeeding mothers have increased from 3.6 million at the beginning of the year to 4.4 million at the six-month point; reported that the overall Plan has the lowest funding for emergency shelter and non-food items at only five percent coverage and that lack of funding in this cluster is expected to worsen conditions for people affected by drought, flooding, conflict, desert locusts and COVID-19 until the end of 2020; notes that failure to meet critical needs will lead to long-term effects that take more resources to reverse and expand the existing socioeconomic gap.

a2355.speaker: Ethiopia Humanitarian Response Plan
a2355.speech: Estimates that 15 million people in the country need urgent assistance, the majority of whom are children and women, and outlines 10 critical clusters, of which the most funded is food at just 67pc coverage.

a2355.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP)
a2355.speech: Says negative coping strategies like reduction and frequency of food, selling productive assets like livestock, and engaging in risky behaviours may also be employed by those in need.

a2355.speaker: Asiya Anfer, displaced person at a campsite in the Afar Regional State
a2355.speech: Said of the health workers: "They are also providing different types of food to the younger children. Particularly the ones they think are sick. They do that through checking their arm."

a2355.speaker: Messay Mulugeta (PhD), associate professor of socioeconomic development, food security & environmental studies
a2355.speech: Said the ever-widening gap in funding for humanitarian assistance is the result of donor countries now directing the resources for the needs of their own citizens due to the impact of the pandemic.

a2355.speaker: Messay Mulugeta (PhD), associate professor of socioeconomic development, food security & environmental studies
a2355.speech: Said: "It is now the time, more than ever, to look within our community for addressing these needs. One method is through food banks that can be set up even in the smallest towns." ; Warned that if these steps are not taken, it could lead to a high death toll due to hunger, in addition to the socioeconomic upheaval that could be brought by stealing and destruction as people find alternate ways to sustain themselves ; Said: "We need to work strongly on fundraising within the country. This could also help eradicate the continued dependence we have on other countries to sustain the basic needs of people in the country."

a2359.speaker: Sir Keir Starmer, UK Prime Minister
a2359.speech: Has recently announced a boost to the UK defence spending, with the increase coming at the expense of the aid budget; explained that the increase will see an additional 13.4bn pounds on defence every year from 2027, but that it will be paid for by cutting development assistance aid.

a2359.speaker: Government of the Netherlands
a2359.speech: Has equally announced a cut to its funding for UN and civil society.

a2359.speaker: Transparency International France, 2022 "Handbook for Asset Restitution"
a2359.speech: Cited the BOTA Foundation as one of the most effective and successful examples of asset return administration.

a2359.speaker: Plaintiffs in the 2009 Wiwa vs. Shell settlement (Kiisi Trust Foundation)
a2359.speech: At the time of the settlement, it was agreed that the Kiisi Trust "should stand as one legacy of the labours of our heroes past."

a2690.speaker: Somali officials
a2690.speech: Announced Thursday that Ambassador Mohamed Ali Nur, widely known as Americo, has been appointed director of Mogadishu Port, replacing Ahmed Mohamed Mohamud, who is commonly known as Washington.

a2690.speaker: Mohamed Ali Nur (Americo), newly appointed Mogadishu Port director
a2690.speech: In his first remarks, Americo underscored the port’s central role in Somalia’s economic recovery. “Mogadishu Port is the lifeline of Somalia’s economy. Our goal is to expand services, ensure accountability, and create an environment that encourages investment and trade,” he said.

a2690.speaker: Somali officials (on outgoing director)
a2690.speech: Officials praised Mohamud for guiding the port through years of instability, citing his efforts to keep operations running despite security risks and global trade disruptions.

a2690.speaker: Somali authorities
a2690.speech: Somali authorities see Mogadishu Port’s development as key to positioning the country more competitively in regional trade.

a2716.speaker: Media reports (unnamed)
a2716.speech: According to media reports, UNICEF will implement the project in close partnership with the Mauritanian authorities in order to ensure beneficiaries' access to sanitation and hygiene services meeting international humanitarian standards.

a2716.speaker: Malinne Blomberg, Deputy Director General of the African Development Bank Group for North Africa
a2716.speech: "This emergency aid illustrates our solidarity with Mauritania and our commitment to protecting the dignity of the most vulnerable populations." ; "By partnering with UNICEF and the national authorities, we are providing a rapid and concrete response to the essential needs of refugees and host communities."

a2716.speaker: Alba Serna, water and sanitation engineer at the African Development Bank
a2716.speech: "This project will improve the health, dignity and safety of thousands of people, while promoting participatory and sustainable management of sanitation infrastructure. It is a decisive step towards strengthening the resilience of the communities of Hodh El Charqui."

a2716.speaker: Mohamed Salem Ould Merzoug, Mauritanian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a2716.speech: declared at the 80th session of the United Nations General Assembly, held in New York, that Mauritania hosts around 250,000 Malian refugees and has recently completed the regularisation of more than 150,000 migrants.

a2732.speaker: Ruth Nankabirwa, Minister of Energy and Mineral Development (Uganda)
a2732.speech: Confirmed that a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed on 22nd December 2023 between the Government of Uganda and Alpha MBM Investments LLC from the United Arab Emirates, outlining cooperation and negotiation terms for the Refinery Project ; said negotiations of the key commercial agreements between the Government and Alpha MBM Investments LLC commenced on 16th January 2024 and are expected to be concluded in the next three months.

a2732.speaker: Ruth Nankabirwa, Minister of Energy and Mineral Development (Uganda)
a2732.speech: Said Alpha MBM Investments LLC has proved that it has money to move forward with the project that is behind schedule ; said that she is praying that the new partner fast-track the process that will lead to the construction of the 60,000 barrels of oil per day (bopd) Greenfield refinery in Hoima.

a2732.speaker: Albertine Graben Energy Consortium (AGRC)
a2732.speech: Had suggested raising some of the money to construct the refinery by listing it on the stock exchange.

a2732.speaker: Engineer Irene Bateebe, Permanent Secretary at the Ministry of Energy (Uganda)
a2732.speech: Said that with the design they are taking with Alpha, they expect that at the time of signing the commercial agreements, a form of Final Investment Decision will be taken: “Because immediately we sign the agreements, we shall see some works commence. So that is an innovative way, the works commence based on the equity of the two partners” ; “And for the National Oil Company, we have already begun programming their equity contribution. They have some portion and for the next financial year 2024/2025, we equally programmed some financial contribution. So they should be able to put on table their equity.”

a2732.speaker: National Oil and Gas Policy for Uganda 2008 (document)
a2732.speech: Recommends refining the discovered oil in country to supply the national and regional petroleum product demand before consideration of exportation.

a2738.speaker: SOS Village d’Enfant (project initiators)
a2738.speech: Say the ‘‘Family Strengthening Programme’’ constitutes an effective tool for the empowerment of families and local communities in the protection of children’s rights, and that it aims at «the empowerment of vulnerable families and local communities in the protection of the Child’s rights».

a2738.speaker: Kadra Mohamed Ali, official of the NGO SOS Village d’Enfant
a2738.speech: In a presentation before officials, stressed that the programme, lasting three years, has received funding of 731,000 euros, or 144,000,000 of our francs, from the German government; she said it targets some «200 families, 1,000 children and 400 young people from the Warabley, Layabley, Moustiquaire and PK12 neighbourhoods of the commune of Balbala» ; insisted that it will make it possible not only to improve the living conditions of families and young people living in Balbala, but that it also intervenes in the area of their resilience through partnership and strengthens the capacities of local associations to protect children and vulnerable families.

a2738.speaker: Fatouma Mahamoud (presentation)
a2738.speech: «The activities to strengthen the capacities and skills of families will be carried out through training of parents or guardians on themes related to the protection of the Child’s rights, parental responsibility, family self-sufficiency, community mobilisation, financial management and the development of micro-enterprise management» ; on community strengthening, indicated that «the programme intends to reactivate the traditional reflex of community solidarity by facilitating the consolidation of community-based organisations (CBOs) so that they allow access to savings and credit for Income Generating Activities».

a2738.speaker: Omar Dileita Mohamed, National Director of SOS Village d’Enfant
a2738.speech: Emphasised the importance of strengthening families to allow every child to grow up in a family environment conducive to its development: «As a child, you need someone who supports you, who believes in you when you are ready to grow and enter the world».

a2738.speaker: Omar Dileita Mohamed, National Director of SOS Village d’Enfant
a2738.speech: «Where children lack confidence, we strengthen their courage and their skills, so they can thrive in the future»: «Today, 1 child and 1 young person in 10 is separated from their family, abandoned, neglected or forced to live in an abusive environment, growing up without the support they need to prepare their future. The effects of this often last a lifetime, creating a harmful cycle that repeats itself from one generation to the next. This happens every day, in every country, city and neighbourhood, even if we do not always see it. Together, we are here to break this cycle and to prevent it from happening in the first place. Where they have lost their voice, we help them find it again. And where they lack confidence, we strengthen their courage and their skills to thrive in the future. That is why we are here».

a2738.speaker: Michael Hausler, Ambassador of Germany to Djibouti
a2738.speech: Recalled the bilateral projects carried out by his country in Djibouti: «For many years, it (Germany) has supported the projects of SOS Children’s Villages in Djibouti (in Tadjourah and Balbala) and the German embassy itself has supported two projects in the area of families in recent months».

a2738.speaker: Michael Hausler, Ambassador of Germany to Djibouti
a2738.speech: «Germany is a strong partner in development cooperation and humanitarian aid in Africa»: «Germany is very happy to finance this project which will bring concrete help. The young people who benefit from the project grow up with access to the tools they need to participate productively in society and in the economic system. For example, the existing E-Learning Center will be expanded to allow more young people to obtain practical training there. In addition, SOS Djibouti will use the premises built during the project for other community development projects. Germany is a strong partner in development cooperation and humanitarian aid in Africa. The greater part of German support for Africa and Djibouti is channelled through European and international organisations».

a2738.speaker: Mouna Osman Aden, Minister for Women and the Family (Djibouti)
a2738.speech: In her address, stressed the importance of the programme for the empowerment of Djiboutian families, women and girls for her department and for the whole Djiboutian government, which according to the minister is in perfect agreement with the human capital development policy of the President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh ; «It is a model that must be supported and accompanied because it is a type of programme that responds to the country’s expectations» ; «What must be understood is that it is a healthy family, in good health and in a favourable environment, that makes a healthy, united society able to move forward in a sustainable environment. (…) Today is 7 November, we are in the month of celebrating the child. It is therefore important for us to be able to say that we are here, so that the Djiboutian child can find their place, in this world, in this city and in this developing country. Every Djiboutian child has the right to their most primary, most fundamental rights. And we have the duty to ensure their protection. For the family strengthening programme, I think it is a model programme of integrated action… the empowerment of the family, of women and the empowerment of the young girl is one of the priorities of the Ministry for Women and the Family, because it is through empowerment that we will be able to reach prosperous development. Today SOS village has taken a step, a stage, in being able to establish a family strengthening programme in Djibouti on the same footing as developed countries. It is an example to follow».

a3146.speaker: Mokgweetsi Masisi, President of Botswana
a3146.speech: Says his government is focused on transforming young people of Botswana into diamonds that will never end ; said he is fortunate to lead a country that is basking in the energy of young people that are ready to take on the challenges of entrepreneurship and embrace opportunities, and that young people are more positioned to create change, as they are wired for innovation and are comfortable with taking risks.

a3146.speaker: Mokgweetsi Masisi, President of Botswana
a3146.speech: Said the new Ministry of Entrepreneurship, announced last week, is expected to bring change in the landscape of entrepreneurship in Botswana in digitization, technology, innovation, disruptions and will enhance connections between local entrepreneurs and those across the world; hopes it will go a long way in guiding young entrepreneurs to take advantage of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), further noting that the population of Botswana is relatively small therefore they should look further afield to expand their businesses.

a3146.speaker: Mokgweetsi Masisi, President of Botswana
a3146.speech: Urged the delegates to never give up, try new ideas and constantly learn new things. “Lean on strong people who have succeeded before you,” he said, adding that entrepreneurs should be frugal.

a3146.speaker: Kgomotso Phatsima, Botswana’s first female military pilot
a3146.speech: Shared with the audience that they have to be ready to venture into unchartered territories. She said if she had allowed her background to stand in the way, she would not be where she is today. “People will tell you that you will not make it. Because I was from a poor background, I was told that I would not make it, but I did.”

a3146.speaker: Emma Wareus, former Miss Botswana
a3146.speech: Concurred that entrepreneurs, especially young entrepreneurs, do not have it easy. She however urged financiers and other business support structures to rather offer assistance in areas where possible. “It is better to say, how would you like us to help you, rather than saying, your idea won’t make it.”

a3231.speaker: Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a3231.speech: Has pledged its commitment to work along with Liberia in the implementation of the five hundred million US dollar Second Compact Grant.

a3231.speaker: Jason Small, MCC Managing Director for Africa
a3231.speech: Said: "The entity will begin recruiting staff with the subsequent establishment of the MCC Office in Liberia, to jumpstart the implementation of the grant" ; speaking on Monday, January 20, 2025, during a courtesy visit to the Finance Ministry, praised the Liberian Government for the progress made in pursuing economic and democratic reforms.

a3231.speaker: Mark Toner, US Ambassador to Liberia
a3231.speech: Described the MCC Second Compact Grant as a win for Liberia; urged the Government and people of Liberia to continue leveraging opportunities for the growth and development of the country.

a3231.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Finance Minister of Liberia
a3231.speech: Has called on Liberians to unite in the face of diversity to move the country forward; said: "The development of Liberia transcends political and social divisions for the greater good of all" ; extolled both current and past governments, including technicians, for their significant contributions to securing Liberia's partnership with the MCC; reaffirmed Liberia's commitment to working closely with the MCC to ensure the entity's Second Compact Grant brings long-term benefits to the country.

a3244.speaker: Ellen Kaosa, Mozambican refugee in Nsanje, Malawi
a3244.speech: Told DW that her group traversed dangerous routes, including across the Shire and Zambezi rivers on a boat, to reach Malawi, and described conditions at the Tengani emergency displacement camp as "problematic": "Since Monday I have not eaten. I have children, and other women are pregnant, elderly and others with disabilities." ; told DW that the congested camp has no toilets, running water or mosquito nets, adding that well-wishers only provided one cup of porridge to some of them upon arrival ; "We are prone to diseases like malaria and waterborne diseases at this time of the rainy season." ; "The whole reason we have fled to Malawi is the safety of our lives, but we plead for help in areas of food, bedding and a place to be accommodated in because it is hot living in tents."

a3244.speaker: Other Mozambican refugee women
a3244.speech: Told DW that they could not find their spouses, fearing they may have taken different routes into Malawi.

a3244.speaker: Dominic Mwandira, Nsanje district commissioner (letter to Malawi's commissioner for refugees)
a3244.speech: "The situation remains dire as these individuals urgently require humanitarian assistance."

a3244.speaker: Human rights campaigners
a3244.speech: Have urged Malawi and the international community to prioritise the well-being of women, the elderly, people with disabilities and children.

a3244.speaker: Moses Mkandawire, human rights defender
a3244.speech: Noted that Mozambican lawmakers and opposition members, along with the 16-member Southern African Development Community (Sadc) and other stakeholders, should work together to foster dialogue, reconciliation and lasting peace: "Now what should we do as a nation, what is needed therefore is to ensure that we provide them with food, blankets and other humanitarian kind of support" ; added Malawi should engage Sadc colleagues in Mozambique for help.

a3244.speaker: Malawian authorities
a3244.speech: Confirmed they are working with the United Nations High Commission for Refugees (UNHCR) to assess the humanitarian support needs of those fleeing Mozambique.

a3244.speaker: Malawi Vulnerability Assessment Committee (report)
a3244.speech: Reports that at least 5.7 million Malawians require urgent food aid by April to avoid descending into debilitating hunger and poverty.

a3244.speaker: Lazarus Chakwera, President of Malawi
a3244.speech: Renewed his appeal for international assistance to address severe food shortages affecting more than one quarter of the country's population of 20 million, saying the country is currently facing one of its worst food shortage situations in decades: "We are not out of the woods yet. This is why I continue to lobby for international support to address the humanitarian crisis we are facing," he said in a televised national address ; acknowledged the donations that Malawi has so far received from various development partners through the U.N. World Food Program and said additional food aid is urgently needed to save lives: "If you are out there standing with Malawians and giving them the help they need during this crisis, I can assure you that Malawians are honest and fair-minded people who will remember those who are bringing them food in this season of drought and hunger, and who know how to distinguish them from those who brought them nothing." ; in March of this year appealed for $200 million in food aid for millions of citizens facing starvation due to a drought linked to the El Nino weather condition.

a3244.speaker: Robert Naija, spokesperson for Nsanje District
a3244.speech: Told DW that Malawi has provided hundreds of bags of maize flour and beans to feed the refugees; added that so far the government has provided shelter to the asylum seekers chiefly in primary schools, however they were being relocated to evacuation centres.

a3244.speaker: Malita Banda, Nsanje resident
a3244.speech: Noted that while Malawians also face hunger due to El-Nino induced weather, the government should increase its budget to meet the demands of those fleeing Mozambique's post-election violence: "My only request is that the Mozambican government should do something as quickly as possible because it is likely that they will have difficulties in finding food to eat on a daily basis."

a3244.speaker: Mozambican opposition
a3244.speech: Denounced the October election result as fraudulent.

a3244.speaker: Constitutional Council of Mozambique
a3244.speech: Said Chapo won the October 9 presidential election with around 65 percent of the vote, with opposition candidate Venancio Mondlane said to have received 24 percent.

a3244.speaker: Venancio Mondlane, Mozambican opposition presidential candidate
a3244.speech: Says the election results were rigged, and said that his fight for a recount is not over and that he will issue a new call for action in the coming days.

a3330.speaker: GCC Ministerial Council (final communique of the 163rd session, Mecca)
a3330.speech: Affirmed the support of the Gulf states for the brotherly Palestinian people in the Gaza Strip and its surroundings, the lifting of the blockade imposed on the Gaza Strip, the alleviation of the suffering of the Palestinian people and the securing of the delivery of humanitarian and rapid assistance to the residents of Gaza, calling for the protection of the civilian population, refraining from targeting them, and for compliance with international law and international humanitarian law without exception; condemned the decision of the Israeli occupation government of 2 March 2025 to halt the entry of humanitarian aid into the Gaza Strip as a serious violation of the ceasefire agreement, international humanitarian law and the Fourth Geneva Convention, and called on the international community to stop these serious Israeli violations, to activate international accountability mechanisms and to ensure sustainable access to aid ; stressed the need to open all crossing points to allow humanitarian aid to enter the Gaza Strip ; called on the Security Council to adopt a binding resolution under Chapter VII of the UN Charter ensuring a permanent ceasefire, an end to the genocide of the Palestinian people and their forced displacement, the entry of humanitarian aid and a return to normal life in the Gaza Strip ; called on the international community to take the necessary measures within the framework of international law to respond to the practices of the Israeli government and its policy of collective punishment against the residents of the Gaza Strip.

a3330.speaker: GCC Ministerial Council (final communique of the 163rd session, Mecca)
a3330.speech: Stressed that Israel bears full responsibility for its violations and attacks on the Gaza Strip, which have led to the deaths of tens of thousands of civilians, the majority of them women and children, and considers them war crimes and crimes against humanity under international humanitarian law ; condemned in the strongest terms the crimes committed by the Israeli occupation forces in the Gaza Strip in the context of crimes of genocide and ethnic cleansing, including the killing of civilians, torture, execution, disappearances, forced displacement and looting, calling on the Security Council to form an independent international committee to investigate these crimes ; condemned the destruction by the Israeli armed forces of residential areas, hospitals, schools, universities, mosques, churches and infrastructure in the Gaza Strip, including the massacre in the Nuseirat camp on 13 December 2024 and the burning of the Kamal Adwan Hospital on 27 December 2024 ; condemned the attacks by Israeli occupation forces on humanitarian and international organisations in the Gaza Strip and the attacks by Israeli settlers on humanitarian aid convoys.

a3330.speaker: GCC Ministerial Council (final communique of the 163rd session, Mecca)
a3330.speech: Positively assessed the outcomes of the extraordinary Arab summit, the "Palestine Summit", held on 4 March 2025 in Cairo; affirmed its support for the Palestinian-Egyptian-Arab plan approved by that summit, stressing that the future of the Gaza Strip must be in the context of a single Palestinian state and the implementation of the two-state solution, welcomed the summit's decision to hold an international conference on recovery and reconstruction in Gaza and called on the international community and all brotherly and friendly countries to participate actively and generously in the reconstruction donors' conference ; stressed the importance of the summit statement's call to establish an international fund for the care of the orphans of Gaza in cooperation with the United Nations ; welcomed the joint statement of the Arab six-party meeting in Cairo on Palestine of 1 February 2025 ; welcomed the outcomes of the Ministerial Conference on Strengthening the Humanitarian Response in the Gaza Strip held in Egypt on 2 December 2024 ; affirmed Security Council resolutions 2735, 2712 and 2720 and the UN General Assembly resolution of 5 December 2024 on a ceasefire in Gaza ; highly appreciated the efforts made by Qatar, Egypt and the United States of America to reach a ceasefire agreement in the Gaza Strip.

a3330.speaker: GCC Ministerial Council (final communique of the 163rd session, Mecca)
a3330.speech: Stressed the central role of the Palestinian cause, the end of the Israeli occupation, and support for the sovereignty of the Palestinian people over all the occupied Palestinian territories, calling on all countries to complete their procedures for recognising the State of Palestine and to take immediate collective measures to achieve a permanent solution guaranteeing an independent Palestinian state on the 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital ; welcomed the recognition by 146 countries so far of the State of Palestine, highly appreciating the leading role of the Kingdom of Spain ; affirmed its support for the efforts of the international coalition to implement the two-state solution and for the Saudi-Norwegian-EU effort to define a timetable for the establishment of an independent Palestinian state ; welcomed the UN General Assembly's decision to hold a high-level international conference in New York in June 2025 chaired by Saudi Arabia and France ; highly appreciated the UN General Assembly resolution of 13 September 2024 on ending the unlawful presence in the occupied Palestinian territories and Palestine's right to full UN membership.

a3330.speaker: GCC Ministerial Council (final communique of the 163rd session, Mecca)
a3330.speech: Condemned the continued construction of settlements in the occupied Palestinian territories and the expulsion of Palestinians from their homes, rejecting any steps to annex West Bank settlements to Israel as a clear violation of the UN Charter, international law, Security Council Resolution 2334 (2016), the 2004 ICJ Advisory Opinion and the Fourth Geneva Convention ; called on the international community to intervene to stop attacks on the Palestinian presence in Jerusalem and attempts to impose Israeli sovereignty over it ; condemned the storming of the blessed Al-Aqsa Mosque by the Israeli Minister of National Security under the protection of the occupation authorities on 26 December 2024 and the repeated storming of its courtyards by settlers and Israeli officials ; condemned the continuing Israeli attacks in the West Bank, including the bombardment of Tammun on 29 January 2025 and of Jenin on 23 January 2025 ; condemned the Israeli occupation's published map showing parts of Arab countries (Jordan, Lebanon, Syria) within its borders, warning that publishing such maps would harm the chances of peace in the region ; highly appreciated the UNESCO Executive Board decision of 16 October 2024.

a3330.speaker: GCC Ministerial Council (final communique of the 163rd session, Mecca)
a3330.speech: Condemned the decision of the Government of Israel of 28 January 2025 to halt the work of UNRWA, calling on the United Nations to fulfil its obligations under international law and to oblige the occupying state to revoke this decision ; welcomed the UN General Assembly decision of 12 December 2024 to request an advisory opinion from the International Court of Justice regarding Israel's decision to ban the Agency's work in the occupied territories, and the General Assembly decision of 5 December 2024 affirming full support for UNRWA's mandate.

a3330.speaker: GCC Ministerial Council (final communique of the 163rd session, Mecca)
a3330.speech: Affirmed its firm position and previous decisions condemning Iran's continued occupation of the three islands (Greater Tunb, Lesser Tunb and Abu Musa) belonging to the United Arab Emirates, supporting the UAE's right to sovereignty over the three islands and their territorial waters, airspace, continental shelf and exclusive economic zone; considering any Iranian decisions, practices or actions on the three islands null and void; and calling on Iran to respond to the UAE's efforts to resolve the issue through direct negotiations or recourse to the International Court of Justice ; condemned Iran's continued construction of illegal colonial housing to settle Iranians on the three islands, the Iranian military manoeuvres and combat exercises on Abu Musa of 20 June 2024, and the repeated visits of senior Iranian officials to the three occupied islands.

a3330.speaker: GCC Ministerial Council (final communique of the 163rd session, Mecca)
a3330.speech: Affirmed that the entire Durra field is located in the maritime areas of the State of Kuwait and that ownership of the natural resources in the divided submerged zone adjacent to the Saudi-Kuwaiti divided zone, including the entire Durra field, is joint property solely between the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the State of Kuwait, and affirmed its categorical rejection of any claims of rights of any other party in that area.

a3330.speaker: GCC Ministerial Council (final communique of the 163rd session, Mecca)
