a6894.speaker: Abdullahi Aden, Director of the Blue Economy at the Ministry
a6894.speech: Said that they have established a strategy to benefit from the blue economy so that the country becomes self-sufficient in the future.

a6894.speaker: FEI Shengchao, Chinese Ambassador
a6894.speech: Spoke in detail about the importance of the relationship between Somalia and China; specifically, about cooperation in the field of fisheries and the Blue Economy, underlining that China is one of the countries that have close relations with Somalia as far as fishing is concerned.

a6894.speaker: Sheri Nauane Duncan-Jones, head of USAID
a6894.speech: “The Somali leadership has demonstrated strong commitment to progress and resilience demonstrating that a bright future for the country is possible. However, as we all know climate change threatens the growth and the competitiveness of key productive sectors in Somalia.”

a6931.speaker: "Christofina" (pseudonym), sex worker from Oshakati and KP-STAR beneficiary
a6931.speech: "I am happy with the programme and have tested negative for HIV, not once - but multiple times" ; "I receive a food voucher that comprises 10 kilogrammes of maize meal, half a litre of cooking oil and a tin of beans. The caseworker also helped my children into another USAID-funded programme for orphans and vulnerable children" ; "Finding money to feed my family is a daunting challenge," she said, as her clients don't pay up well as the pandemic continues to contribute to food insecurity of certain communities, affecting her and her clients.

a6931.speaker: Jessica Long, Chargé d'Affaires of the US embassy to Namibia
a6931.speech: "The KP-STAR programme also identifies children who are living with female sex workers and links them to psychosocial support, social welfare, and programmes designed to improve their economic skills."

a6931.speaker: USAID (Namibia)
a6931.speech: In Namibia, USAID strongly believes in "people-level impact" and supports the health ministry to build a sustainable response to the HIV epidemic.

a6968.speaker: Mabugu et al., 2013 (study)
a6968.speech: Cited as showing that the South African Revenue Service (SARS) modernised tax processes, improving compliance and funding public programmes, such as healthcare and social grants.

a6968.speaker: IRS, 2022 (report)
a6968.speech: Cited as showing that the United States' Internal Revenue Service enables the US government to collect the revenue needed for federal programmes like Social Security and Defence.

a6968.speaker: OECD, 2021 (report)
a6968.speech: Cited as showing that Germany's Finanzamt, known for its efficiency, supports a strong welfare state, including free healthcare and education.

a6968.speaker: Rousseau (social contract theory)
a6968.speech: The social contract, a concept developed by thinkers like Rousseau, argues that citizens give up certain freedoms, such as paying taxes, in exchange for protection, services and public order provided by the State.

a6968.speaker: Friedman, 2021 (study)
a6968.speech: Cited as showing that when citizens evade taxes, they weaken the social contract, resulting in poor public services and deteriorating trust in the government.

a6968.speaker: Hawkins, 2009 (study)
a6968.speech: Cited on Zimbabwe's collapse: tax evasion and economic mismanagement led to hyperinflation, failing hospitals and crumbling infrastructure.

a6968.speaker: OECD, 2017 (report)
a6968.speech: Cited on Greece's debt crisis: chronic tax evasion played a major role in Greece's financial collapse, forcing austerity measures that hurt its citizens.

a6968.speaker: Reuters, 2023
a6968.speech: Cited as reporting that Namibia banned the export of unprocessed critical minerals such as lithium and cobalt in 2023 to encourage local value-addition.

a6996.speaker: Peter Canterbury, Managing Director of Triton Minerals
a6996.speech: “Shandong is historically the only large-flake graphite producer in China and is expected to see significant drops in graphite production as their assets age and mines are closed due to environmental impacts which the government are looking to reduce.”

a6996.speaker: Peter Canterbury, Managing Director of Triton Minerals
a6996.speech: Notes that Mozambique is one of the few countries in Africa that don't require a free-carry interest in their mines, and whose regulatory codes are transparent: “We are also situated only 80 km by sealed road to the Pemba port, eliminating any challenges around exporting our product” ; on the adjacent graphite mine owned by Germany's largest graphite products producer, in operation since 2016: “Consequently, the area has developed a good reputation for its high quality graphite.”

a6996.speaker: Peter Canterbury, Managing Director of Triton Minerals
a6996.speech: Confirms that Ancuabe's full-capacity output of 60,000 tpa of graphite material, which may seem small, is in fact on the larger size of graphite production; notes the mine will operate for 28 years although there is a substantial 49 Mt resource which once converted could either ramp up the facility's operating rate or drastically increase the project's lifespan ; “Importantly, we have determined a four-year payback on the project and a 37% IRR.”

a6996.speaker: Peter Canterbury, Managing Director of Triton Minerals
a6996.speech: “We have planned for a 15-month construction period which will take us to July 2021 to produce our first graphite.”

a6996.speaker: Peter Canterbury, Managing Director of Triton Minerals
a6996.speech: Explains that Ancuabe will comprise two pits - the T16 deposit and then later on the T12 deposit - situated just 3 km apart: “With our graphite situated no deeper than 130 m, the deposits will be open cut, drill and blast operations. The material will be transported to a ROM pad which will be followed by three crushing stages after which it will be moved into a temporary holding bin, ready for processing.”

a6996.speaker: Peter Canterbury, Managing Director of Triton Minerals
a6996.speech: “We will also benefit financially from a 110 kVa power line that runs through our tenement after it has been upgraded in 2022.”

a6996.speaker: Peter Canterbury, Managing Director of Triton Minerals
a6996.speech: “With 50% of our product already secured by end users, and the necessary funding in place to take Ancuabe through to production, we believe we are a stand-out graphite junior and are positioned to soon move from developer to producer” ; “In doing so we will deliver value through returns which will give us the optionality of returning cash to our shareholders through dividends or developing the additional assets in our portfolio.”

a7103.speaker: Omar Hilale, Permanent Representative of Morocco to the United Nations
a7103.speech: Firmly defended the legitimacy of the kingdom to represent Africa as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, arguing that the candidacy is part of a strategic vision and a lasting commitment to multilateralism and international cooperation ; In an interview with the Moroccan news agency MAP, stressed that Morocco, under the leadership of King Mohammed VI, has asserted itself as a central and respected actor in the defense of pan-African causes, and recalled the deep and constant commitment of the Moroccan sovereign to the continent, reflected in active solidarity with the majority of African states ; "Morocco is eligible to become a member of the Security Council because the fundamental criterion is to contribute to global peace and security, particularly through participation in peacekeeping missions" ; Highlighted the unique expertise of the Royal Armed Forces, stemming from their in-depth knowledge of African cultures and languages, as well as their involvement in social initiatives for local populations ; Stressed Morocco's adherence to universal principles and international rules and its respect for the United Nations Charter, and highlighted Morocco's bilateral and trilateral initiatives focused on mediation, cooperation and humanitarian assistance, citing concrete examples where the kingdom has intervened to strengthen stability and development in Africa ; "Given its continued commitment to promoting peace, security and sustainable development, Morocco has the necessary assets to occupy a permanent seat on the UN Security Council in the future."

a7178.speaker: Fixer and interpreter in Fujian, a university graduate who asked to go unnamed (anonymous)
a7178.speech: Kept talking about the matter. “The Chinese government will do nothing,” he said. “But we should go to war.”

a7178.speaker: Official records
a7178.speech: Confirmed the death toll at Nanjing at between 250,000 and 300,000.

a7178.speaker: Various Japanese nationalists
a7178.speech: Have continued to claim over the decades that the figure has either been widely exaggerated or fabricated for the purposes of propaganda.

a7178.speaker: Shintaro Ishihara, governor of Tokyo
a7178.speech: As recently as February of this year, said he believed the massacre never happened — it would have been impossible, he reportedly said, to kill so many people in such a short timeframe.

a7178.speaker: New York Times
a7178.speech: Noted of the incident: “Wen Jiabao, the Chinese prime minister, refused to meet with his Japanese counterpart, Naoto Kan, and threatened Japan with ‘further action’ if it did not unconditionally release the fishing boat's captain. The Chinese government also blocked exports to Japan of a crucial category of minerals used in products like hybrid cars, wind turbines and guided missiles. It even detained four Japanese… The dispute may strengthen the military alliance between the United States and Japan, as did an incident in April 2010 when a Chinese helicopter buzzed a Japanese destroyer. Such confrontations tend to remind Japanese officials, who have suggested that they need to refocus their foreign policy on China instead of America, that they rely on the United States to balance an unpredictable China, analysts say.”

a7178.speaker: Wen Jiabao, Chinese prime minister
a7178.speech: Refused to meet with his Japanese counterpart, Naoto Kan, and threatened Japan with “further action” if it did not unconditionally release the fishing boat's captain.

a7178.speaker: Washington Post
a7178.speech: Reported that one man draped the Japanese flag over his dog during the protest outside the Japanese embassy in Beijing.

a7178.speaker: Los Angeles Times
a7178.speech: Reported that in Guangzhou, on 16 September, demonstrators stormed into the first two floors of a complex that houses the Japanese consulate, breaking windows in a hotel and smashing a vehicle.

a7178.speaker: 22-year-old woman from Hunan Province (interview subject)
a7178.speech: She told us that she had taken Japanese as a second language at high school, and that she never wanted to speak it again.

a7178.speaker: Japanese Prime Minister
a7178.speech: Called on Beijing to ensure protection of his country's people and property.

a7454.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Nigeria's Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare
a7454.speech: Announced, on Channels Television's Hard Copy programme, that the government is working to absorb the 28,000 health workers previously paid through USAID into the country's healthcare system and reduce reliance on foreign aid; acknowledged the significant contribution of the US government to Nigeria's healthcare sector, particularly in HIV, Tuberculosis and Malaria, but emphasised that Nigeria is determined to take ownership of its healthcare sector: "There are health workers, 28,000 of them, who were being paid through US government support. While it has been appreciated, those health workers are Nigerians. We have to find ways to transit them."

a7454.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Nigeria's Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare
a7454.speech: Said about 70 per cent of the country's total health expenditure comes from private sources, including out-of-pocket payments: "Our total health spends in Nigeria, the total health expenditure: 30 per cent is public, 70 per cent is private" ; noted external assistance is not the primary source of Nigeria's health funding: "The component of overseas development assistance for health is not the largest chunk of our health expenditure."

a7454.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Nigeria's Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare
a7454.speech: Stressed the need for increased domestic investment in healthcare, citing President Bola Tinubu's Renewed Hope Agenda, and highlighted the government's recent approval of nearly $1 billion: "We've seen deliberate efforts to mobilise resources to invest in health. Just last week, the Federal Executive Council approved almost a billion dollars in terms of financing for the programme. That is a significant resource that states will implement. It's a programme for results that will deliver better, but it will take time."

a7454.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Nigeria's Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare
a7454.speech: Highlighted Nigeria's heavy dependence on imports for pharmaceutical needs: "Can you believe that more than 70 per cent of our drugs, we import with foreign exchange that we didn't have? So, if we can flip it over time. 99 per cent of our medical devices, we import them" ; "Now, if we flip that over time, that is not going to take place overnight, but we have to be on that path" ; "Healthcare is not cheap. Quality healthcare is not cheap. You have to invest in it. We as a country had not invested in it, and yet we had been asking for the highest quality health."

a7454.speaker: American president's team, led by billionaire Elon Musk
a7454.speech: Saying they are auditing the agency (USAID) to check waste and corruption in the system.

a7454.speaker: Nigerian Senate
a7454.speech: Recently allocated an additional N300 billion to the health sector in the 2025 budget, expected to take care of the 28,000 health workers, among other issues in the sector.
